instruction: Optimize this spreadsheet for printing by resizing all cells so the entire content fits on one page, then save as PDF. Use the same filename as the original spreadsheet and place it in my home directory.

metadata.explanation: Alternative wording focusing on print optimization. Same evaluation criteria: PDF must exist at specified path, contain 1 page, and have reasonable file size.
metadata.verification_details: Uses existing check_pdf_pages metric to verify: (1) PDF file exists at /home/user/Resize_Cells_Fit_Page.pdf, (2) PDF has exactly 1 page (relation=eq, ref_value=1), (3) PDF file size > 10KB (verify_content=True). No custom functions needed as check_pdf_pages is already available in desktop_env.evaluators.metrics.pdf.

llm_judge_reasons: The verify_content=true flag causes check_pdf_pages to check for images in the PDF (pdf.py:47-58), but LibreOffice Calc exports spreadsheets as text/vector graphics, not images
The image check will likely cause false negatives - the evaluator will fail even when the task is completed correctly
The semantic verification logic is incorrect for spreadsheet-to-PDF conversion tasks
File size check (>10KB) is reasonable, but combined with the image check makes the evaluator unreliable
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Remove verify_content flag or set it to false - the basic checks (file exists, 1 page) are sufficient for this task
Alternatively, modify check_pdf_pages to skip the image check for spreadsheet-originated PDFs, or add a flag to control whether image verification is needed
The current implementation at pdf.py:47-58 assumes PDFs should contain images, which is semantically incorrect for text/data document conversions

rule_validation_issues.msg: metric check_pdf_pages first parameter type (str) may not match getter get_vm_file return type (Union)
